title: On Jumping over the ditch in one stride
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：jump　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 jump 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the tailor ① jumped over the ditch in one stride in the rain, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② jumps over the ditch in one stride without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ jump over the ditch in one stride at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ jumped over the ditch in one stride before — a line in the order for November 1942 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Jumping over the ditch in one stride in the rain, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ jump to twice the old sum without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Jump to twice the old sum at once and never mention it again.

By 1955 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ jumps to twice the old sum in the rain every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ jumped over the ditch in one stride again when nobody else would.

⑩ To jump over the ditch in one stride, my mother said in 1960, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody jumps over the ditch in one stride without complaint again and somebody must jump over the ditch in one stride in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 跳（一般过去式 jumped over the ditch in one stride：1948 年裁缝头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 跳（一般现在 jumps over the ditch in one stride：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 跳（不定式 to jump over the ditch in one stride：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 跳（过去完成时 had jumped over the ditch in one stride：1942 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 跳（动名词 jumping over the ditch in one stride 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 猛增（jump to twice the old sum：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去猛增猛涨到从前的两倍）
G. v. 猛增（jump to twice the old sum：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 跳（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 jumps to twice the old sum，而母亲又一次 jumped over the ditch in one stride）

answers.why: jump 意为“跳”，1948 年裁缝淋着雨跳一步跨过那条沟，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 jumped。
jump 意为“跳”，自那以后裁缝毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 jumps。
jump 意为“跳”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯跳一步跨过那条沟”，此处为不定式 to jump over the ditch in one stride。
jump 意为“跳”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1955 年之前就有人跳过，故用过去完成时 had jumped。
jump 意为“跳”，裁缝说“跳一步跨过那条沟这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 jumping over the ditch in one stride 作主语。
jump 意为“猛增”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去猛增猛涨到从前的两倍”，should ever 之后用原形 jump to twice the old sum。
jump 意为“猛增”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻猛增猛涨到从前的两倍（jump to twice the old sum at once），以后再也不要提起。
jump 意为“跳”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例猛增猛涨到从前的两倍，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 jumps。
jump 意为“跳”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨跳一步跨过那条沟，用一般过去式 jumped 叙述。
jump 意为“跳”，结尾那句是母亲 1960 年的话：要跳一步跨过那条沟，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。

多年以后，裁缝仍毫无怨言地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（jumps over the ditch in one stride）

早在 1942 年就有人跳一步跨过那条沟，十一月那天订单簿上的一行字就是证据。（had jumped over the ditch in one stride）
裁缝说过，淋着雨跳一步跨过那条沟这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（jumping over the ditch in one stride 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻猛增猛涨到从前的两倍，以后再也不要提起。（jump to twice the old sum，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 jump 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the tailor jumped over the ditch in one stride in the rain, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor jumps over the ditch in one stride without complaint whenever the shop asks.
Jumping over the ditch in one stride in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever jump to twice the old sum without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop jumps to twice the old sum in the rain every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother jumped over the ditch in one stride again, and the shop remembered that half.
